gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: 'The delay is your fault,' the manager said to her. The manager ___ her for the delay.
gaps.explanation: Blame takes the pattern blame somebody for something.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Sit down, please,' the nurse said to me. The nurse asked me ___ down.
gaps.explanation: Requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive: asked me to sit down.

gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget to lock up,' my mother said. My mother reminded me ___ up.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' corresponds to remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I don't like seafood,' he confessed. He confessed that he ___ like seafood.
gaps.explanation: Present simple negative backshifts: don't like → didn't like.
